answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity continuously prove useful work: a rotating beacon assigns each agent random, verifiable computation jobs, and only agents that return correct results on time keep their standing. Each job is a vertex in a graph of earned trust, not an ivory tower credential that can be bought in bulk; an identity with no history of completed work is a relic that earns nothing. A sybil farmer must therefore pay real compute for every fake identity, and mass fakes starve because one machine cannot finish many time-boxed jobs at once.
